text:
nora: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing a controlled migration from current per-tenant token quotas to an SLO-prioritized credit allocator. Wanted to surface tradeoffs and get ops + infra alignment. Link to RFC: https://rwg/reviews/slo-credit-migration :eyes:

ben: skimming — high level I'm +1. main question: do we keep hard per-route caps as a safety net during rollout, or rely solely on soft credits?

nora: good Q. proposal is 3 phases: (1) soft-credit overlay (no hard caps), (2) soft credits + emergency hard caps per-tenant (configurable), (3) cutover to credit-first admission with legacy caps only for enforcement during incidents.

liam: prefer keeping small hard caps early. we saw abuse cases where soft signals alone didn't contain bursty scraping.

zoe: ops perspective: hard caps need simple rollback knobs. also we need per-route AND per-key visibility in the console before phase2. otherwise support gets flooded.

maya: telemetry ask: add per-credit-allocate histograms and rejected-by-credit counters. need to track SLO impact (p50/p95 latency) correlated with credit burn.

infra-bot: NOTE: moving to credit allocator requires a schema change in token-store: add credit_bucket_id and last_refill_at (nullable). migration window recommended: 48h rolling backfills.

ben: tradeoffs: soft credits reduce tail latency for small bursty tenants, but complicate fairness when tenants backpressure. How do we handle tenant priority weights vs SLO weights?

nora: plan: compute effective_score = tenant_weight * slo_weight / (1 + recent_burn_rate). scheduler ranks by effective_score when admitting across congested shards. keeps priority but penalizes hot tenants.

liam: sounds reasonable. question on implementation boundary: should the effective_score calc live in admission-service or the per-shard scheduler?

zoe: keep it in admission-service. admission-service has global view and can attach score as admission hint; shard scheduler can still use hint but maintain local fairness if hint absent.

maya: config snippet for rollout we discussed:

```
admission:
  mode: overlay
  credits:
    refill_interval_s: 60
    default_refill: 1000
    emergency_hard_cap: 20000  # per-tenant tokens
  scoring:
    slo_weight: 0.7
    tenant_weight_map:
      small-startup: 0.8
      enterprise: 1.2
```

liam: we should also emit a per-tenant "degradation_reason" tag when we throttle so product can explain to customers (and we can wire to billing if needed).

ben: abuse prevention: RFC suggested anomaly scoring using request-pattern entropy + embedding-similarity sample. that's compute heavy. ops ask: can we make a cheap first-pass heuristic (rate window + repeated route variance) to mark candidates and only run heavy checks on flagged tenants?

nora: yes, two-tier detection: cheap heuristics -> mark candidate -> expensive ML check async (and attach signal to credit allocator). candidates get temporary stricter refill until cleared.

ops-bot: ACTION: create runbook for emergency_hard_cap rollback and monitoring thresholds (assigned: zoe). ETA: 3d.

zoe: noted. I'll draft the runbook and include the dashboard/widgets for per-tenant credit burn, recent_burn_rate, effective_score, and rejects_by_policy.

maya: instrument edges: we need a single tag in traces from admission-service so Console can join traces to the scheduler decisions. add "admission.score" and "admission.decision" span tags.

liam: migration concerns: long-lived tokens in DB — how do we backfill credit_bucket_id for tokens that haven't been used in months? do we create buckets lazily on first use or backfill?

nora: lazy creation on first use to avoid heavy DB churn. infra-bot note warned of a 48h backfill option for tenants we proactively enable.

ben: maybe add a "prewarm" path for high-value enterprise tenants that pre-allocates buckets and sets higher default_refill. avoids 429s during rollout.

nora: agreed. add prewarm list to rollout checklist. also will prepare the migration feature flag that gates admission overlay.

zoe: last ops point: ensure dedicated and private deployments can opt out or configure different default_refill/hard caps. enterprise customers will expect predictability.

nora: yes, plan includes per-deployment overrides in config API.

maya: final: will prototype telemetry dashboard widgets and add alerts: (1) rise in rejects_by_policy > 0.5% of requests, (2) median credit refill latency > 200ms, (3) effective_score skew across shards > 3x.

nora: thanks all. next steps: ben to review scoring formula details, zoe to own runbook + dashboard, maya to own telemetry protos, liam to prototype admission hint interface with shard scheduler. checkin in 72h. :rocket:
